questions.question: A user asks "what day is 103 days from today?" and the app has separate get_current_date_time and add_duration_to_date_time tools. Why does this require multiple tool calls in sequence rather than one?
options: Claude first needs today's date from one tool before it has enough information to call the second tool that adds the duration
The API enforces a hard limit of one tool call per tool per conversation
Each tool can only return one field, so results must be split across calls
Claude always calls every available tool once regardless of relevance

questions.question: Why must an application that wires up tool use be structured as a loop (submit, check for tool_use, run and resubmit, repeat) rather than a single request/response?
options: A user query can require an unpredictable number of chained tool calls before Claude has enough information to answer
The Claude API requires exactly two round trips for every tool-enabled request
Loops are only needed when using the text editor tool
Streaming responses always require a while loop to render tokens

questions.question: What is the recommended way to detect whether Claude wants to call a tool, rather than manually scanning the response content blocks?
options: Check the stop_reason field on the response for the value tool_use
Check whether the response text is empty
Check the HTTP status code of the response
Check whether more than one content block was returned
